```r
###############################################################################
# TrainSel installation
###############################################################################
#
# TrainSel contains compiled C++ code. Before running the R installation code,
# install the development tools required by your operating system.
#
#
# WINDOWS
#
# Install the Rtools version corresponding to your version of R:
#
# https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/
#
# Use the default installation options, then restart R or RStudio.
#
#
# macOS
#
# TrainSel supports both Intel Macs and Apple Silicon Macs, including
# M1, M2, M3 and M4 processors.
#
# 1. Install the version of R appropriate for your Mac:
#
#    Apple Silicon -> arm64 version of R
#    Intel Mac      -> x86_64 version of R
#
#    https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/
#
# 2. Install Apple Command Line Tools by running this command in Terminal:
#
#    xcode-select --install
#
# 3. Install the GNU Fortran compiler recommended for your version of R:
#
#    https://mac.r-project.org/tools/
#
# For official R 4.5 installations, use:
#
#    gfortran-14.2-universal.pkg
#
# The universal installer supports both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs.
#
# Restart R or RStudio after installing the development tools.
#
# Do not normally edit ~/.R/Makevars. Old compiler settings in this file can
# interfere with the compiler configuration supplied by R.
#
#
# LINUX
#
# On Ubuntu or Debian, install the required development tools with:
#
#    sudo apt update
#    sudo apt install build-essential gfortran
#
###############################################################################


###############################################################################
# Run the following code in R or RStudio
###############################################################################

options(
  repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"),
  timeout = 600
)

# Packages needed to install and run TrainSel
required_packages <- c(
  "Rcpp",
  "RcppArmadillo",
  "RcppEigen",
  "RcppProgress",
  "foreach",
  "doParallel",
  "remotes"
)

missing_packages <- setdiff(
  required_packages,
  rownames(installed.packages())
)

if (length(missing_packages) > 0L) {
  install.packages(
    missing_packages,
    dependencies = TRUE
  )
}

# Install TrainSel from GitHub
remotes::install_github(
  repo = "TheRocinante-lab/TrainSel",
  dependencies = TRUE,
  upgrade = "never",
  build_vignettes = FALSE
)

# Load TrainSel and confirm the installed version
library(TrainSel)

cat(
  "\nTrainSel was installed successfully.\n",
  "Installed version: ",
  as.character(packageVersion("TrainSel")),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


###############################################################################
# Troubleshooting
###############################################################################
#
# Successful installation normally ends with:
#
#    * DONE (TrainSel)
#
# Compiler warnings do not necessarily indicate installation failure.
# The important information is found in the final lines of the output.
#
#
# Windows
#
# If compilation tools are not found, confirm that the Rtools version matches
# the installed version of R. Restart RStudio after installing Rtools.
#
#
# macOS
#
# If the error mentions:
#
#    C++14 compiler required
#
# confirm that TrainSel/src/Makevars contains:
#
#    CXX_STD = CXX14
#
#
# If the error mentions:
#
#    /opt/gfortran
#    emutls_w
#    gfortran
#    Fortran libraries
#
# install the GNU Fortran compiler recommended for the installed version of R:
#
#    https://mac.r-project.org/tools/
#
#
# Users can check their system architecture in R with:
#
#    Sys.info()[["machine"]]
#    R.version$arch
#
# On a native Apple Silicon installation, both should indicate arm64.
#
#
# When reporting an installation problem, provide:
#
#    1. The operating system
#    2. The R version
#    3. The output of R.version$arch
#    4. The first line containing "error:"
#    5. The final 30 to 50 lines of the installation output
#
###############################################################################
```
